Dr. Keith Reisinger-Kindle was sued by a woman who alleges he left part of a fetus inside her during an abortion.

Associated Press file photo

Share

A lawsuit alleging a Champaign doctor botched an abortion was settled last month.

Dr. Keith Reisinger-Kindle was accused of leaving part of a fetus inside a woman and puncturing  her uterus while performing an abortion  at Champaign-based Equity Clinic in April 2023. When she started experiencing extreme cramping, Reisinger-Kindle allegedly told her to take Tylenol and laxatives.

The woman sued Reisinger-Kindle and Equity Clinic in March 2025. They reached a settlement on July 8, according to the News Gazette newspaper in central Illinois.

The woman’s lawyer at the Chicago firm McNabola & Associates declined to comment. Reisinger-Kindle’s lawyers at Pretzel & Stouffer did not respond to a request for comment.

The woman, a mother of four, was about 22 weeks along when she sought an abortion from Reisinger-Kindle, according to her suit. Two days after the procedure, she was still experiencing cramps, so she went to the emergency room.

That’s when doctors found parts of a fetus in her right pelvis and surgically removed them. Doctors also found a hole in her uterus about the size of a quarter, according to the suit. Reisinger-Kindle allegedly refused to answer questions or share information with one of the surgeons who operated on the woman.

In July 2025, Reisinger-Kindle was disciplined by the state and fined $5,000. He also had to complete 20 hours of continuing medical education for failing to properly evaluate a patient.
